I really wanted to enjoy *Assassin's Creed Unity*, but the controls completely ruined the experience for me. They're clunky, unresponsive, and often make the character do the opposite of what you intended.

The biggest issue was a frustrating bug where, after playing for a while, Arno would get stuck in stealth mode and refuse to move properly. The only way to fix it was to restart the game, and even then it would eventually happen again.

Between the awkward controls and the recurring bugs, the game became more frustrating than fun. It's a shame because the world and visuals are great, but the gameplay issues make it hard to recommend.

# 🎮 Assassin's Creed Unity... the game that could've been one of the GOATs. 😭 (8/10)

After finally finishing **Assassin's Creed Unity**, I honestly don't even know how to feel about this game. 😅 It's one of those games that makes you say **"I love it"** and **"I hate it"** at the exact same time.

## ✅ The good stuff

First of all... **the graphics are INSANE.** 🤯✨

Seriously, even after all these years this game still looks better than a lot of modern games. Paris is absolutely gorgeous 🗼 and the amount of detail is just crazy.

One thing I loved is that you can actually enter random houses. 🏠 It makes the world feel so much more alive. Even tiny details are amazing. Sometimes Arno randomly says **"Sorry"** to NPCs after bumping into them. 😂 It's completely unnecessary... but that's exactly the kind of detail I love seeing in games.

The **combat** looks awesome too. ⚔️ If you've played every Assassin's Creed game in release order, you'll definitely notice the new assassination animations. They look clean, brutal and satisfying. 🗡️💀

The **parkour** is probably one of the best parts of the game. 🦅 It adds some new tricks and the animations are just beautiful to watch. Half the time I wasn't even doing missions... I was just running across rooftops because it looked so good. 😂

The music also deserves some love. 🎼 Some songs you hear inside taverns honestly reminded me of **Black Flag**, and as someone who loved that game... it gave me some serious nostalgia. 🏴‍☠️

Now the story...

**10/10.** ❤️

I genuinely loved it. It's emotional, keeps you interested the whole way through and yeah... the ending is pretty sad. 😢 But if you've been playing Assassin's Creed for years, you kinda expect Ubisoft to break your heart at the end anyway.

## ❌ Now... the bad stuff.

...

Where do I even start? 💀

I swear I could write an entire book just about the bugs in this game. 📖🐛

Seriously...

This game is **SO BUGGY** it's actually impressive sometimes.

Combat bugs. ⚔️🐛

Parkou…

This is the last real "Assassin's Creed" game. I enjoyed the combat since it was a bit more complex than other AC's so enemies could actually overwhelm you when they had the numbers. But at the same time, the combat can be a bit slow which is annoying sometimes. The parkour is smooth and fluid. I must admit that it is better than both older and newer AC titles. So it was definitely worth it to complete the main story. The setting in France is cool and it is filled with random activities/encounters. If you look at the outfits/cosmetics; Unity has by far the cleanest drip compared to most AC's. 

But then the main reasons why i stopped playing after completing the main story; The storyline itself and the protagonist/characters. I will describe the story in 1 word; Boring. Nothing else to say about it. A washed version of Ezio from Ebay named "Arno" who simps on a girl named Elise (she isnt even good looking at all lol).

Conclusion; The last AC game that truly gives you the assassin feeling and vibe. Enjoyable, but not great.

I've played almost every single Assassin's Creed bar Origins and Shadow, and have been playing them since Revelations released, this is the single worst Assassin's Creed game I have ever had the displeasure of dumping my time into. 

I initially thought the hate for this game was overblown, and to an extent I think a very small amount of it still kind of is, but, it still has so many problems that just claw anything good it does down to a D-tier game. 

The phantom blade is told to be a virtually silent weapon allowing for undetectable assassinations from afar, but I clearly had to have been given the cow bell variety. As any time I had thought was a perfect time to use it, every guard in a 50 mile radius immediately locks onto me through walls and ruins any attempt at stealth I made. Even removing any stealth combat, guards having clear X-ray vision was such a problem my entire playthrough, real stealth became frustrating.

The combat was way too slow and floaty, the finisher animations could never really decide if they wanted to allow my parry attempts or not so any real combat was extremely hit or miss. 

The story was unbelievably meh and they quite literally drop the overarching Animus storyline at the end so nothing gets resolved or comes from the entire game that you just played. Up until sequence 9 things were fine and I was willing to look past the faults, but around there things just start to fall apart like a cliff of sand.

When the parkour decides it wants to work, it looks pretty good, probably the flashiest in the series with the most animations. The problem is more than half the time it decides that Arno should have a seizure instead of jumping to the next hold, or follows an input you put in three business days earlier, ruining the entire flow and just makes it a slog. The game also crashed a lot, but im willing to cut a little bit of slack because im traveling and…

citations.review_text:
Assassin's Creed Unity is a very solid and very fun Assassin's Creed game. The parkour, combat, and side content are some of the best in the entire series so far and Paris is potentially my favorite city in Assassin's creed. I LOVE how lively and active the streets are, with thousands of protesters filling out the streets of revolutionary Paris.

Unfortunately this game's story is quite week in comparison. Arno is quite weak as a character and really just feels like diet Ezio for the first couple sequences, but the story after that just kinda meanders and doesn't get interesting until near the end of the game. It's a shame that this story isn't better, because AC Unity would absolutely be a 9/10 if it was.

Still a great game and a really fun time. 

8.5/10

# 🎮 Assassin's Creed Unity... the game that could've been one of the GOATs. 😭 (8/10)

After finally finishing **Assassin's Creed Unity**, I honestly don't even know how to feel about this game. 😅 It's one of those games that makes you say **"I love it"** and **"I hate it"** at the exact same time.

## ✅ The good stuff

First of all... **the graphics are INSANE.** 🤯✨

Seriously, even after all these years this game still looks better than a lot of modern games. Paris is absolutely gorgeous 🗼 and the amount of detail is just crazy.

One thing I loved is that you can actually enter random houses. 🏠 It makes the world feel so much more alive. Even tiny details are amazing. Sometimes Arno randomly says **"Sorry"** to NPCs after bumping into them. 😂 It's completely unnecessary... but that's exactly the kind of detail I love seeing in games.

The **combat** looks awesome too. ⚔️ If you've played every Assassin's Creed game in release order, you'll definitely notice the new assassination animations. They look clean, brutal and satisfying. 🗡️💀

The **parkour** is probably one of the best parts of the game. 🦅 It adds some new tricks and the animations are just beautiful to watch. Half the time I wasn't even doing missions... I was just running across rooftops because it looked so good. 😂

The music also deserves some love. 🎼 Some songs you hear inside taverns honestly reminded me of **Black Flag**, and as someone who loved that game... it gave me some serious nostalgia. 🏴‍☠️

Now the story...

**10/10.** ❤️

I genuinely loved it. It's emotional, keeps you interested the whole way through and yeah... the ending is pretty sad. 😢 But if you've been playing Assassin's Creed for years, you kinda expect Ubisoft to break your heart at the end anyway.

## ❌ Now... the bad stuff.

...

Where do I even start? 💀

I swear I could write an entire book just about the bugs in this game. 📖🐛

Seriously...

This game is **SO BUGGY** it's actually impressive sometimes.

Combat bugs. ⚔️🐛

Parkou…

Playing this game for the first time, and my god Im impressed. There are many times where crowds just make me stop and say wow. Almost no modern games even come close, only Saber's engine comes close. The world is beautifully rendered and holds up on max settings(Turn off Nvidea stuff if you have AMD cards for a 2x fps boost). Story is leagues better than the last two outings from AC, and hell Im enjoying this game far more than AC Black Flag resycnced.

This is the most "assassin" experience I've seen in the series. Great gameplay and customization. Blackbox assassinations are amazing and they require you to actually plan what you're doing. The story is lacking and treats most of the revolution as a background instead of incorporating Arnos story with it. The story is grounded but can still be enjoyed if you want to see Arnos personal revenge plot. The graphics are insanely good for a 2014 game and the lightweight RPG elements are actually enjoyable and don't feel like a hassle. The star system and no level gating makes it a game I would actually put time into upgrading my character for. The combat system is one of my favorite in the series except the guns are just way too overpowered and enemies have dead-accurate precision. Arnos character is complex but for a few sequences at the beginning it feels like he isn't even there due to lack of dialogue or character in cutscenes, Luckily this is resolved in the later sequences.

Story: 7.5/10
Characters: 8.5/10
Gameplay: 9.5/10
Open-World: 9/10
Overall: 8.5/10

Also Ubislop fix your launcher.

Time for some brutal honesty.

What can i say about Assassin's Creed: Unity...
It's a mixed bag but I would say that there are way more positives than negatives.
Let's start with the story, it's lack-luster, Arno doesn't feel very compelling as a protagonist and is driven mainly by venngence. Follows the same structure as most AC games, search, tail, kill, listen etc.

World design is the best part about the game, the city of Paris feels lived in, every street feels like it has a story to tell. The amount of  models they manage to pack into the streets without your PC crashing is amazing, it really adds to the atmosphere. I spent hours just walking around, soaking in the environment.

The attention to historical detail is also fantastic, I found myself reading newspapers and every new database entry just because I found them so interesting.

Gameplay is fun, especially combat, the kill animations are fantastic and brutal, never get tired of seeing them, probably some of the best animations in the series. Parkour just doesn't live up to the hype, it's janky and frustrating. 

Overall experience is still well above average and I really enjoyed my time playing Unity.

This game overall was pretty fun! Absolutely stunning and immersive visuals, audio, everything, the most npc’s I’ve ever seen in a game that are all doing unique animations and activities, I often found myself just standing there watching npc’s do stuff, such amazing attention to detail! And the buildings, streets, lighting, textures, everything is so well crafted and detailed even in 2026 I’m still in awe! Gameplay-wise there is some clunkiness with the parkour and some gameplay feels less smooth, but overall good fighting/stealth mechanics. 

After a while the game feels a little empty and the quests that are not the main story feel a little repetitive. It’s also just very city heavy, if that makes sense, I wish it were like half city, half French country side. Because after being in the city so long in, it becomes hard to figure out where you are and everything just blends together and sometimes I got sick of seeing building everywhere. Lastly, I would also say that the story was just OK, left a little bit more to be desired but wasn’t terrible.

 I would recommend Assassin’s Creed: Unity as I feel It’s still a solid entry in the Assassin’s Creed franchise: 6.5/10

Assassins Creed Unity is visually stunning, especially when it comes to the massive crowds. Paris looks incredible, and the setting of the French Revolution is easily one of the game's strongest aspects. Sadly, the gameplay and technical issues hold it back.

The gameplay becomes repetitive very quickly and rarely evolves beyond the same gameplay loop. The story never managed to hook me, and the relationship between Arno and Élise which is supposed to be the emotional core of the game never felt believable or engaging.

What frustrated me the most, however, was the parkour system. It looks spectacular, but it often does the exact opposite of what you want. Arno jumps in the wrong direction, climbs walls you never intended to climb, or simply ignores your inputs. As a result, even basic movement feels unnecessarily imprecise.

Despite all the patches over the years, the game is still surprisingly buggy. There are plenty of visual glitches, but also game breaking bugs that can cause missions to fail. For example, if you get shot while climbing, Arno can become stuck floating in mid air, unable to move. Using the rope lifts can sometimes clip you inside buildings you're not supposed to enter, leaving you trapped. I've also had cutscenes fail to load, leaving me with nothing but audio playing over a black screen. And that's just scratching the surface.

The LOD (Level of Detail) distance is also set far too low, resulting in constant and noticeable pop ins. During cutscenes, buildings in the background often switch to extremely low detail models and textures, which is very distracting and hurts the presentation. You can manually edit the games .ini file to improve this, but its baffling that theres no ingame graphics option to adjust the LOD distance in the first place.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a heavy grind, requiring significant time investment to unlock and upgrade equipment.

citations.review_text:
Overall, this is an ok game. It is frustrating because it is difficult to find info on the missions you have accepted if you split off one and do another. It is also VERY "grindy". You repeat what seems to be the same mission over an over. 

Of course, it also suffers from the standard AC issue of climbing stuff or NOT climbing stuff when you do/don't want to. You are pointed to a clear path, with something climbable next to it and you will, about 50% of the time, climb it rather than just keep running. Or you WANT to climb it, but it won't. By this point, I would have thought that AC would have figured out a way to intuit what you are trying to do based on which way you are POINTING the camera.

Finally, it can be difficult to figure out what it next. Thank goodness for internet-based clues.

Anyway, it's an AC and fairly good. If it weren't for the climbing bugs and the grindiness, I'd give it a wholehearted recommendation. It is still recommended, but barely. Especially if it isn't on sale.

[h1] A Step Forward for the Series...? [/h1]

Firstly, I have to not recommend this title because, despite it being a game from 2014 & my PC parts being substantially newer than the game, somehow, this game manages to completely lock-up Windows 11.  The bad kind of lock-up where you need to hard reset the machine! I had this occur twice in a row specifically during a main-mission (involving a bottle of wine).  There were other instances as well, which seemed to occur more frequently the further I progressed in the game. Thus, there's likely a memory leak of some kind in the game's code.  

Additionally, the addition of paid-only-in-game-currency is a huge red flag to me for future titles in the series.  While yes, you can technically unlock everything (except the time-saver packs) with the other non-paid-currencies in the game,  the amount of grinding / game-time required to unlock & upgrade all pieces of equipment is deliberately long in order to try and bait you into buying 'Helix Credits'.  

Now for the game itself; somehow they managed to make free-running harder to control and finicky over previous titles.  Trying to free-run through windows at times seemed to be a battle in itself (despite holding the correct inputs down).  The main-missions and assassinations in said missions are fun and even unique, fresh experiences this time around which is a huge plus.  Arno & Elise are likeable, good characters that you find yourself caring about (unlike, say, Shay from the previous title).  However, the main story is far shorter than the side content and the side content isn't nearly as interesting.  Co-op is fun, when you can find people to play with, but that too feels half-done.  There's not enough co-op missions in the game, and the solution Ubisoft decided was to make it so each co-op mission needs to be played 3 times to unlock everything.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the stealth system is inconsistent, with detection meters that can rapidly escalate and enemies spotting players through walls and smoke.

citations.review_text:
I've put an unreasonable amount of time into this game. Both on PC and on PS4 (where it ran like ass). I don't think this is the best Assassin's Creed has to offer. In terms of progression, I'd play 4 or rogue. For story I'd play 2. For combat, I would play literally any other game besides Assassin's Creed.

This game is very stylish youtube compilations, but you will quickly discover how actually jank it is. The parkour snap points are scuffed. Climbing in windows only works 70% of the time. The free run up and down does offer a bit more control than other games, but it's a little confusing at times where it will lead you.

Stealth is very inconsistent. Detection meter can explode on a dime and force you into combat. 

Combat itself is weird, it's full of bugs. The game gets confused at times whether you should be in stealth or just out-of-combat, so it will frequently hang up. You'll be unable to attack and just take hits until the game decides to work again.

Fun with friends I guess.

The parkour, the murder mystery side missions and the co-op (provided you have one or more friends) are the best parts of the game but are painfully dragged down by the severe lack of polish. The funny bugs are gone but the unfunny bugs will always be here. The other good parts are the world design and graphics. 

The game really punishes you for not using stealth and getting into combat, which makes sense, but the detection system is buggy as all hell since they can see you through walls and smoke sometimes, leading to the insanely frustrating combat system which is by far the worst part about the game. There's also a common bug where Dorian will not throw a bomb despite playing the throw animation. The assassination animations are also very inconsistent, some are quick, some take far longer than it should. And this really messes with the rhythm of the missions, especially if you're trying to stay undetected. The story is below mediocre, the characters are too. The dialogue sounds like it was written by AI before AI was a thing and the main character straight up sucks. Dorian never evolves past any personal motivation until the very last cutscene (which is just a low effort monologue) and spends the entire game yelling "Elise Elise!". Fun fact, the dlc has a mission where you trail a regular person without being detected, and after you're done, it turns out that person detected Dorian at some point anyway. And of course, the exploration is mid, which is typical of Ubisoft.

I picked this game up for $7, and for that price, I'd say it's worth it, more so because I had a friend to play with. But anything above $10 is absolutely not, especially since the far superior Black Flag remake is almost here.

citations.review_text:
I hate this game with every fiber of my being, yet here i am after 133h and having all achievments.
I cannot recommend this game at all, this game is filled with bugs to the brim.
i think if you only play the story you might have some decent fun but everything else is just such a horriable experince.

Good grief this is can be a right hassle to play. There are certain bugs that crop up - in movement, or random enemy character freezes, or bizarre animation loops - which can wreck a mission just before completion, in which case you have to replay it all. It is so frustrating, and ultimately I decided it wasn't worth the bother of finishing the game. 

It looks pretty, but the gameplay bugs are only part of what ruin things. There's the Assassin's Creed bollocks about genetic memories and modern-day computer waffle which wreck the immersion (and have done since the very first game). The AC series is a set of fine historical action games fighting against its own storytelling. AC:Unity is also somewhat spoiled by the voice acting. For some reason, most of revolutionary France consist of Cornish yokels with "oo-arrr!" accents which is just... no. 

I wish I could like this game, and much of the time it plays okay. It's just that when it goes wrong, it goes very wrong. For me the last straw was being told to 'knock out the guards', when such a mechanic has not been introduced before and I have no idea what to do. I cannot complete the game. 

Sometimes, you have to remind yourself of the sunk costs fallacy: just because you've put dozens of hours into a broken game, doesn't mean you need to waste more trying to finish it. Ca ira!

The parkour, the murder mystery side missions and the co-op (provided you have one or more friends) are the best parts of the game but are painfully dragged down by the severe lack of polish. The funny bugs are gone but the unfunny bugs will always be here. The other good parts are the world design and graphics. 

The game really punishes you for not using stealth and getting into combat, which makes sense, but the detection system is buggy as all hell since they can see you through walls and smoke sometimes, leading to the insanely frustrating combat system which is by far the worst part about the game. There's also a common bug where Dorian will not throw a bomb despite playing the throw animation. The assassination animations are also very inconsistent, some are quick, some take far longer than it should. And this really messes with the rhythm of the missions, especially if you're trying to stay undetected. The story is below mediocre, the characters are too. The dialogue sounds like it was written by AI before AI was a thing and the main character straight up sucks. Dorian never evolves past any personal motivation until the very last cutscene (which is just a low effort monologue) and spends the entire game yelling "Elise Elise!". Fun fact, the dlc has a mission where you trail a regular person without being detected, and after you're done, it turns out that person detected Dorian at some point anyway. And of course, the exploration is mid, which is typical of Ubisoft.

I picked this game up for $7, and for that price, I'd say it's worth it, more so because I had a friend to play with. But anything above $10 is absolutely not, especially since the far superior Black Flag remake is almost here.
